purpose: deep-dive on pair 4 (go-flutter/bookmarks-app), the one task both arms failed in the completed nine-pair battery

root_cause.failure: go test -race: TestConcurrentVisits fails with 'race detected during execution of test' in both arms, both runs
root_cause.explanation: The mutex correctly guards the POST /bookmarks/{id}/visit increment (bm.Visits++), but bm is a *Bookmark pointer into the shared store and writeJSON(w, http.StatusOK, bm) marshals it AFTER s.mu.Unlock() -- a concurrent visit's write can race with this goroutine's read during JSON encoding. Fix would be to copy the value (resp := *bm) or encode while still holding the lock.
root_cause.spec_note: local-model-bench task spec explicitly calls this out: 'This is the primary concurrency stress point: many concurrent visits to the same bookmark must all be counted (no lost updates).' Both baseline and hardened-harness independently wrote the same class of bug -- a genuine 27B-model concurrency-reasoning gap, not something targeted by either harness fix (nested-manifest verification, stale-context handling).

runs.source: standalone rerun, same task and arm order, to rule out stochastic result

reproducibility: Both arms failed with the identical race-condition failure signature across two independent runs -- this is a consistent capability limit for this task, not a stochastic one-off.

harness_token_breakdown.note: run_screening.py's prompt_tokens is a cumulative sum of usage.input + usage.cacheRead + usage.cacheWrite across every assistant turn in the session, so the large total does not mean that many tokens were freshly computed -- APC (automatic prefix caching) on the :8080 route serves most of a growing session's repeated prefix from cache.
harness_token_breakdown.interpretation: Only ~4.4% of the reported prompt-token total was fresh compute; APC absorbed the rest. The real cost of this outlier session is not ~490K tokens of fresh GPU work -- it's sustaining a large, continuously-growing KV cache resident for the session's full ~37-turn, multi-minute duration, which is the more plausible driver of host memory pressure during a long multi-hour battery than raw token throughput. sum_cacheWrite=0 is unexplained (expected at least an initial prefix write) and worth checking against ai-stack's own APC accounting rather than assumed to be a real gap.
